name: Earliest 16th-Century Monasteries on the Slopes of Popocatepetl
description: Fifteen early monasteries are scattered across Morelos, Puebla and Tlaxcala, in the foothills of the Popocatépetl volcano in central Mexico. Franciscan, Dominican and Augustinian friars built them in the 1500s to convert the local population. Each has a vast open-air courtyard with small corner chapels, where Mass was held outdoors. This design became a model for missions across Mexico and beyond.
